messages:
sasha: Quick sync — we're finalizing the AWS KMS setup for Redwood Private (VPC). Two asks: RBAC mapping for control-plane -> KMS access, and a safe rotation/rewrap flow for dataplane DEKs. Any gotchas?

devin: @sasha putting notes here from the infra side. main constraints: control-plane runs in customer VPC (customer-managed subnet) and uses an IAM role we assume via STS. We should restrict KMS key policy to that role + our control-plane principal. Avoid wildcard principals. :lock:

caroline: RBAC: prefer least-privilege IAM + KMS key policy. Keep separate roles for control-plane admin vs runtime signer. Admin can schedule rotations, runtime can GenerateDataKey/Decrypt only. Map them in our RBAC system so ops UI shows who can trigger rotation.

devin: Sample key policy we used in a PoC (trimmed):
```json
{
  "Version":"2012-10-17",
  "Statement":[
    {"Sid":"AllowControlPlaneUse","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-private-controlplane"},"Action":["kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:Decrypt"],"Resource":"*"},
    {"Sid":"AllowAdmin","Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-private-kms-admin"},"Action":["kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion","kms:RotateKey","kms:CreateGrant","kms:ListGrants"],"Resource":"*"}
  ]
}
```

devin: Note: we scoped principals to account and role name. For BYOK customers we let them provide the key ARN and we add a grant instead of altering their key policy.

ops-doug: Regarding rotation/rewrap: Recommend automated rewrap pipeline that does: 1) create new CMK (or use rotation if enabled), 2) create grant for control-plane role, 3) re-encrypt DEKs in small batches with backoff, 4) keep old CMK enabled for decrypt for fallback window (7 days default), 5) then retire. Do not delete old CMK immediately.

caroline: Audit logging: Enable CloudTrail KMS events + log to a customer-controlled S3 bucket / Lake. Also emit structured audit events from control-plane when we call GenerateDataKey and Decrypt (include key_arn, operation, request_id, principal_role, dataset id). Tie those to our internal trace_id for incident triage.

mike: Incident playbook notes: if a CMK is compromised (suspected access outside expected roles): 1) immediately disable key (not delete), 2) fail-open dataplane to a fallback compatible model (see fallback policy), 3) trigger internal page and customer notification per SLA, 4) run rewrap across affected DEKs to new CMK, 5) rotate credentials and review grants. Keep a forensic snapshot of CloudTrail + VPC flow logs. :rotating_light:

sec-bot: Automated check: found 2 keys in test account with `KeyRotationEnabled=false`. Recommend enabling rotation or documenting why rotation is disabled.

sasha: @devin can you paste the rewrap command we used in the PoC for batching? ops needs it for the runbook.

devin: Sure — we used a small lambda-driven worker that calls `Encrypt` with the new CMK to rewrap the plaintext DEK. High-level snippet:
```bash
# pseudocode
old_cipher=$(aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://dek.enc --key-id $OLD_CMK --query Plaintext --output text | base64 --decode)
new_cipher=$(echo "$old_cipher" | aws kms encrypt --key-id $NEW_CMK --plaintext fileb://- --query CiphertextBlob --output text)
# store new_cipher back to secret store
```

devin: Important: do not expose plaintext DEKs to logs. Use memory-only buffers, zero them after use, and ensure the worker runs in ephemeral environment in the VPC.

caroline: Grants vs key policy: prefer grants for short-lived runtime access (they're easier to revoke and audit). Key policy changes require owner access; grants can be created by a principal with kms:CreateGrant and are visible in ListGrants. Include GrantToken in requests when doing immediate use after create.

ops-doug: For performance: reuse GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext for re-encryption where possible, and do rewrap server-side if cloud provider supports it. For AWS KMS, decrypt/encrypt is typical. Throttle by RPS and add jitter.

mike: For cross-account BYOK: we must ensure key policy explicitly allows our role and include aws:PrincipalOrgID or explicit ARN. Also ensure we don't request ScheduleKeyDeletion on customer-owned keys. For BYOK, recommend grants only.

sasha: Compliance ask: can we retain enough audit info to show to auditors without leaking DEKs? We need proof of who triggered GenerateDataKey and the key ARN, timestamps, and an operation id.

caroline: Yes — log only metadata. Example event fields to persist: {operation, key_arn, principal_arn, request_id, trace_id, dataset_id, outcome}. Never log plaintext or full ciphertext_blobs.

sec-bot: FYI — added alert rule: KMS API calls from non-whitelisted IPs for control-plane roles -> page on high severity.

devin: One more gotcha: when using CMK auto-rotation, AWS rotates the key material for the same logical key id. That doesn't automatically rewrap customer DEKs — you still need to re-encrypt data with new data keys if you want to switch envelope key; however with GenerateDataKey you can choose CMK rotation or create new CMK and rewrap. Document the distinction in the runbook.

sasha: Plan for next steps: (1) dev implements key policy + grant pattern in terraform module, (2) ops write rewrap lambda skeleton and tie to runbook with safe gating, (3) sec reviews audit retention and alerting, (4) schedule tabletop for compromised CMK scenario. I'll open PRs and assign owners.

mike: I'll take the tabletop and incident notifications. ops-doug take the rewrap pipeline. @caroline can you review the RBAC mapping doc once devin pushes the terraform?

caroline: yep. will review and add control-plane UI hooks for the admin actions.

devin: I'll push terraform module this afternoon — will include sample key policy and grant creation flow.

sasha: Great — thanks all. Leaving notes here for the runbook. :white_check_mark:
